evaldash would flicker on refresh and temporarily clear the loaded
models & metrics which sucked.

#### Agent Description

Keep the model picker and comparison results visible while background
requests run. Previously, the 60-second poll and returning to a visible

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[shellbox] Mount explicit read-only roots in local machines (#9955)

`LocalMachineFactory` now mounts exactly the host directories it is
given in `read_only`, read-only at their own paths, alongside the system
directories. `bin_dirs` only sets `PATH`. The factory no longer follows
a venv's `python3` to the interpreter install it resolves to, or
recreates the symlinks on the way (#9954). A symlink that leads outside
the mounted directories does not resolve in the sandbox, so each
`read_only` directory must be self-contained. A `read_only` path that is
not an existing directory raises `ValueError` when the factory is
created.

`build_python_environment(root, lock, python_version)` in
`shellbox.backends.local.python_environment` builds such a directory
with uv. It installs a managed CPython of the given full version under
`root/python`, creates a venv at `root/venv` from it, and runs `uv pip
sync --require-hashes --link-mode copy` with the lock. The venv refers
to its interpreter by absolute path inside the root, so the root must
stay where it was built. An exclusive `flock` on a file beside the root
and a completion marker let several processes on a host share one build.
A root without the marker is removed and rebuilt. A finished root built
from another lock or Python version raises `ValueError`. A failed uv
command raises `UvError` with uv's error output.

Tests that run Python in the sandbox share one environment built per
session and skip only when uv reports that it failed to download CPython
3.12.13.

#9798 adds a task-curation local runtime that runs `uv venv` and `uv pip
sync` itself and passes only `bin_dirs`. It will move to `read_only` and
this builder after this lands. The builder does not add that runtime's
packages or NLTK data; the caller adds them after the build returns.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[shellbox] Recreate a venv's interpreter symlinks inside the sandbox (#9954)

uv links a venv's `python` through a minor-version alias directory
(`cpython-3.12-<platform>`, a symlink to the patch-versioned install).
The local backend mounted only the resolved install into the sandbox, so
inside it the venv's `python` link dangled. The shell then fell through
`PATH` to the system interpreter, and commands ran without the venv's
packages on any host whose venv was built on a uv-managed Python; on the
task-curation workers this made about a fifth of grader trials fail with
`ModuleNotFoundError`.

`LocalMachineFactory` now walks the symlink chain from each venv's
`python3` to its interpreter, keeps the links that lie outside the
mounted roots, and recreates them in the sandbox with `bwrap --symlink`.
A test builds a venv whose interpreter path goes through an alias
directory and checks the command runs with the venv's prefix.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[shellbox,verifyit] Local grading backend and typed candidate grading (#9936)

Library changes split out of #9798 so the RL data pipeline PR carries
only the pipeline.

Shellbox gains a `local` backend: commands run as subprocesses of the
host process for trusted scripts that need no container. Each command
gets a scrubbed environment, a privilege drop when the host is root,
process-group kill on timeout, and best-effort lockdown through
no_new_privs, rlimits, and Landlock filesystem and TCP rules. A machine
empties its owned roots per use and may write shared roots that outlive
it. Iris machines accept a command user matching the container's own
user and exit promptly on the stop signal. Docker machines create the
working directory the spec names.

Verifyit grades typed candidates against a mode's spec and the task's
resources through `grade_candidate`, so in-process callers no longer
rebuild a workspace. Pytest grading reports collection and bootstrap
failures as task errors, requires every listed test id to map to a
distinct reported case, and runs setup in the workspace under the shared
deadline.

Part of #9798.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Fuse the expert dSwiGLU and skip recomputed pre-activation stores (#9834)

Two changes to the routed experts' QuACK kernels, each bitwise or within
bf16 rounding:

| Change | Kernel | Hero step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SwiGLU backward and the routing-weight row dot in the dh GEMM's
epilogue | 3.54 ms against 5.10 ms per expert chunk | 13.059 to 12.943 s
(+0.89%) |
| No gate/up pre-activation store in a forward whose residuals are
recomputed | 6.14 ms against 6.48 ms per median chunk, 96 chunks per
step | 12.652 to 12.611 s (+0.33%) |

The expert MLP backward wrote dh = dy @ W2^T to HBM and read it back
with the gate/up pre-activations in an elementwise pass for the SwiGLU
backward and the row dot <h, dh>. A QuACK epilogue on the grouped dh
GEMM now unpacks the interleaved (gate, up) tile, applies the SwiGLU
backward to the fp32 accumulator, writes the packed (d_gate, d_up) and
reduces the row dot, so dh is never materialized. Outputs, drops and dW2
are bitwise unchanged; dx, dW13 and dS change at bf16 rounding (median
~1 ulp), because the SwiGLU backward runs on the unrounded accumulator.

Under the hero's layer remat, the forward's gated GEMM wrote the [C, 2I]
pre-activations of every chunk, which the backward recomputes.
`_routed_experts` declares `optimize_remat`, so such a forward runs a
primal that calls the expert MLP's new `apply`, which returns the output
alone, and the gated GEMM gains a launcher that never writes the
pre-activations. Each chunk's dispatch still waits on the previous
chunk's gate/up output. The forward is bitwise unchanged, and removing
the change from all of #9708 slowed the step by 0.47%.

Step times are single runs on one 64-GPU hero rack (restore step-180000,
seed 0, 100 steps) from #9708's measurements.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Compute the MoE routing-weight gradient on the expert side (#9833)

With QuACK's expert MLP, the ragged all-to-all MoE takes its
routing-weight gradient from the expert MLP's own backward, so the
backward needs neither the expert outputs nor their return transport,
and the hero saves the routed output instead of recomputing the expert
down projection, the return all-to-all and the combine. The step
shortens by 4.12% (13.541 to 13.005 s against #9832, over 26 scored
steps). Peak HBM rises to 125.4 GiB of the 143.75 GiB pool.

The backend chooses the gradient together with its expert MLP kernel;
`moe_mlp` takes no option for it. QuACK's expert MLP (SM100, SiLU, QuACK
installed) takes the expert-side gradient for bfloat16 and float32
tokens, which is the hero's configuration. The portable `ragged_dot`
expert MLP takes the exact gradient, <dout, y> over the kept expert
outputs: it keeps y anyway, so the expert-side gradient would save it
only the returned [TK, H] buffer and the return transport. QuACK with
float16 tokens takes the exact gradient too. The expert-side gradient is
zero at a zero weight, and zero or inexact wherever |w * dout| falls
below the cotangent dtype's smallest normal number: 2^-126 in bfloat16
and float32, which only output cotangents near underflow reach, and
2^-14 in float16, which ordinary magnitudes reach. The hero's routing
weights are positive renormalized sigmoids and its cotangents bfloat16.
Forward, dx, dW13 and dW2 are bitwise unchanged; the routing-weight
gradient differs at bf16 rounding (median ~1 ulp) at nonzero weights.

The gradient with respect to the combine weight w[t,k] is dS[t,k] =
<dout[t], y[t,k]>, the only backward consumer of the expert down
projection's output y. Since dy = w * dout and dh = dy W2^T, the same
value is rowsum(dh * h) / w, built from tensors the expert MLP backward
already holds. One custom VJP from dispatch to combine returns s = <h,
dh> per expert row, sends it back with one [C, 1] f32 all-to-all per
chunk, and forms dS = s / w in f32; dropped and padded slots get 0 by
selection. The backward's transports reuse the forward transfers'
offsets, swapped, and on GPU its weighted output cotangents come from
#9832's scatter kernel.

The saved routed output fits the 114 GiB remat budget that #9831 gives
the carry offload; the backward needs ~105 GiB. With the backward's
transports no longer ordered after the recompute's, several collectives
in flight gave run-to-run different gradients or hung on GB200, so every
ragged run forces a collective overlap limit of 1.

Step times are single runs on one 64-GPU hero rack (restore step-180000,
seed 0), each head compiled fresh.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Leave ragged MoE transport rows unwritten when nothing reads them (#9832)

The ragged all-to-all MoE stops zero-filling and overwriting transport
rows that no consumer reads, and on GPU builds its dispatch buffer with
one scatter. Outputs, drops and gradients are bitwise unchanged. One MoE
layer's forward and backward is 4.4-4.8% faster and its compiler temp
1.37 GB smaller, and the hero step shortens by 1.41% (13.732 to 13.541 s
against #9831, over 26 scored steps).

The expert chunks write disjoint rows of the dispatch and return
buffers, but the custom VJP around `ragged_all_to_all` differentiated
each write as an overwrite, so every layer's backward spent a [TK, H]
select, add and zero fill on rows the next chunk would ignore. Each
written row holds nothing before its one write, and for such a row an
overwrite has the derivative of an add, so the transpose passes the
output cotangent through unchanged. With every consumer reading only
rows a collective wrote, the buffers need no fill: on GPU they come from
a Triton kernel that writes nothing, elsewhere they are zero-filled.
Each buffer is tied to a loop-carried value, because XLA would otherwise
hoist an input-free buffer out of the layer loop and copy it into every
layer's output slot. Dropped and padded slots get combine weight 0, and
the combine and dispatch-gradient sums skip them. A GPU test fills every
buffer with NaN instead of zero and requires identical outputs, drop
counts and gradients under 22 routings, among them an expert no token
selects, a receiver chunk and a whole receiver with no rows, a sender
with only padding, and near-total drops, with two chunks of three
experts per GPU as on the hero.

On GPU, a Triton kernel builds the expert-sorted dispatch buffer by
reading each token's row once and writing it to the token's accepted
slots, where a gather read every row topk times: 0.535 ms (6.6 TB/s) at
the hero's per-GPU routed shape (TK = 524288 rows of the 3072-wide
latent). Its weighted form serves #9833's backward. The gather-sum's
forward loops over 1024-wide hidden tiles, which keeps more programs
resident: 0.508 ms against 0.574 ms.

Step times are single runs on one 64-GPU hero rack (restore step-180000,
seed 0), each head compiled fresh.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Correct hero remat and collective scheduling; build PGLE profiles (#9831)

Carry-offloaded hero runs stop recomputing ~10 GiB of backward values
per step that already fit in HBM, which shortens the step by 1.04%
(13.874 to 13.732 s against #9830 on one 64-GPU hero rack, restore
step-180000, seed 0, 100 steps). Ragged runs without the carry offload
run their collectives one at a time, and `pgle_profile` builds an XLA
PGLE profile from one trace of the train step. No model code changes.

With the layer carry offloaded to pinned host memory, XLA's
`HloRematerialization` charged the 36 GiB carry stack against the device
memory limit and recomputed values that fit (143 remat clones, 0.63
s/step of compute). The launcher now defaults
`--xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading=true` whenever the carry is
offloaded, so remat counts host buffers as host memory. Only the remat
pass reads the flag, after scheduling and copy insertion, so it cannot
reorder the carry reload against its consumer. The flag also lets remat
offload values to host itself when its estimate of the step exceeds its
budget, and that path aborts compilation in XLA's `OffloadInstruction`
(hlo_rematerialization.cc:2118) when it picks the operand of a
collective still in flight. At memory fraction 0.75 and slop factor 85
the budget is 87.7 GiB and remat estimates the step at 96.8 GiB, so the
hero crashed at compile. The carry offload therefore also defaults to
0.78 and 105, a 114 GiB budget, and remat then leaves the step alone
("Rematerialized 0 instructions").

A ragged run without the carry offload keeps the latency-hiding
scheduler off, and the collective overlap limit binds only that
scheduler, so XLA's default scheduler can start two ragged transports at
once. Compiled for a mocked EP64 topology, the program does so in the
forward and in the backward, and on GB200 several collectives in flight
have hung the ragged transport or given run-to-run different gradients.
The launcher now forces
`--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` for that
configuration.

XLA's default latency estimator gives every collective the same small
latency, so with one collective in flight it treats a multi-millisecond
ragged transport as hidden under one GEMM. A profile built by
`pgle_profile` from the program's own trace shortened the hero step with
all of #9708 from 12.611 to 12.515 s (+0.77%). A profile applies only to
the program it was traced from, so nothing uses one by default; the
README describes the trace, build and rerun loop, and #9879 tracks using
one in production.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[dependencies] Fix notebook and virtualenv security alerts (#9918)

Upgrade Notebook to 7.6.3 and JupyterLab to 4.6.4 to fix clipboard-cell
cross-site scripting in [Notebook alert
#707](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/security/dependabot/707)
and [JupyterLab alert
#706](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/security/dependabot/706).
Upgrade virtualenv to 21.7.13 to fix activation-script command injection
through [Windows prompts
(#704)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/security/dependabot/704)
and [bash/fish paths
(#705)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/security/dependabot/705).

Notebook 7.6.3 requires JupyterLab >=4.6.4, so the JupyterLab 4.5.11
security backport cannot satisfy the paired upgrade. Raise the workspace
security floors. Add jupyter-builder 1.0.2 for the notebook
applications; add python-discovery 1.6.0 and update filelock to 3.24.2
for virtualenv's new requirements. Preserve unrelated locked packages.

The lockfile passes `uv lock --check`. The Notebook, JupyterLab,
virtualenv, and pre-commit CLIs report the expected versions. Fresh
virtualenv creation and a pre-commit Python hook passed; relocated Bash
activation printed the missing-path warning without executing command
substitution embedded in the environment path. Windows and fish
activation were not executed locally.

The safe root suite reached 2,385 passing tests before an isolated SkyRL
launcher test failed to install its pinned native Finelog package on
macOS ARM64. The same test fails on the unchanged base commit.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Exit instead of hanging when a June train step stalls (#9903)

GrugTrainerConfig.step_timeout arms Python's faulthandler timer around
each train step
except the first one in the process, which compiles, and watch steps,
which can compile a variant. If a step runs past the timeout, the
process dumps every thread's traceback and exits with status 1. The
default is None, which leaves training unchanged. The synthetic
benchmark sets it with --step-timeout: 300 s by default, 0 disables it.

When one GPU fails inside a step, for example because the BFC allocator
cannot place the step's temp buffer, the other GPUs wait in XLA's
per-step collective rendezvous. On ROCm with JAX 0.11 that rendezvous
never times out. The Python thread blocks on the step's outputs, and the
job sits until its Slurm time limit. In a forced out-of-memory run with
the flag, the job exited 120 s after the out-of-memory error.

Stacked on #9852, which adds the neighboring --watch-interval flag.

Part of #9812

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Require NVIDIA before the SM100 check in ragged all-to-all (#9777)

The ragged all-to-all MoE backend checks for an SM100 GPU before
choosing the QuACK grouped-GEMM expert MLP, and parsed the device's
`compute_capability` as a float. ROCm devices report an architecture
name such as `gfx942`, so every expert-parallel run with `--moe-impl
ragged_all_to_all` on AMD failed with `ValueError: could not convert
string to float: 'gfx942'` while tracing the first step. The check now
requires an NVIDIA device before it reads the compute capability, and
other GPUs fall back to `ragged_dot`, as non-Blackwell NVIDIA GPUs
already do.

The backend still does not run on ROCm. With this change, the June
Snowball model on 8× MI300X (JAX 0.11, ROCm 10) compiles and then fails
in the first step with `UNIMPLEMENTED: Device communicator is not
implementing`, which points to XLA's RCCL communicator lacking ragged
all-to-all. The `ring` and `fixed_all_to_all` backends run on the same
node.

Part of #9462.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[haliax] Run the ragged_dot custom VJP test at highest matmul precision (#9922)

`test_triton_custom_vjp_routes_backward_through_triton_layouts` now
computes both of its paths under
`jax.default_matmul_precision("highest")`. With Triton monkeypatched to
`jax.lax.ragged_dot_general`, the test compares the custom VJP's value
and gradients against XLA autodiff of `ragged_dot(...,
implementation="xla")` at rtol 1e-5, then checks the exact list of
layouts passed to the Triton call.

On MI300X (gfx942, JAX 0.11.0, ROCm 10) the test failed in 5 of 5 runs
in job 454691, in 1 run in job 454775, and in 9 of 10 runs in job 454927
on `main`. The failing assertion varied between the value, the input
gradient, and the weight gradient. The exact loss is 4693.8768. The
failing runs compared 4693.877 against 4690.7314, a relative error of
6.7e-4.

At default precision, f32 dots on MI300X can run on xf32 matrix
instructions, and XLA's GEMM autotuner decides per process whether they
do. On this backend XLA lowers each of the test's dots to a Triton GEMM
fusion. The autotuner then times candidate tile configs and keeps the
fastest. In job 454942, optimized-HLO and LLVM IR dumps from a fully
exact run and a fully reduced run showed:

- Exact run: every dot used a tile with N=8 (e.g. 16x8, 2 warps). The
kernels used scalar FMA and no MFMA instructions.
- Reduced run: every dot used a tile with N=32 (e.g. 16x32, 4 warps).
The kernels lowered `tl.dot` to `llvm.amdgcn.mfma.f32.16x16x8.xf32`.

Over 40 processes in the same job, the output tile size predicted the
result for every dot. All 70 dots with an N=8 tile were exact. All 50
dots with an N=32 tile had 4.7e-4 to 7.7e-4 relative error.

| Autotuning | value exact | dlhs exact | drhs exact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default, 20 processes | 12 / 20 | 12 / 20 | 6 / 20 |
| `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`, 20 processes | 20 / 20 | 20 / 20 | 0 /
20 |

With autotuning off, every process uses the same configs, so results
stop varying, but the drhs config it picks still loses precision. We did
not measure the timing gap between configs. Timing noise on these tiny
shapes is the likely reason the pick changes between processes. The
padded 512-row XLA call in the test lost precision in 8 of 8 earlier
probe runs (job 454926). Under `highest`, all paths were exact in 8 of 8
runs. The same applies outside this test: any default-precision f32 dot
that XLA lowers to a Triton GEMM fusion on MI300X can differ by about
1e-3 relative between runs of the same program. We have not checked dots
that XLA sends to hipBLASLt.

With the change, the test passed 10 of 10 runs on MI300X (job 454928)
and 3 of 3 on MI350X (gfx950, job 454929). Tolerances are unchanged. The
exact call-list assertion passed under JAX 0.11.0 whenever the numeric
checks passed, so this PR leaves it unchanged.

Part of #9812

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Add remat, watch and pooled-wave flags to the June benchmark (#9852)

Add the June synthetic benchmark flags used for the MI350X measurements
in #9812.

The synthetic benchmark supports `--remat-mode
{recompute_all,save_moe}`. At batch 8, `save_moe` reduced step time from
0.716 s to 0.610 s while using 10 GiB more memory
([results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6025360841),
jobs 453346-453411). `--watch-interval N` sets the gradient watch
interval; 0 turns off the watch step. Turning it off reduced batch 8
peak memory from 164.3 to 150.2 GiB. The batch 8-64 sweep used this
setting
([results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6026123091),
jobs 453351-453384).

The benchmark also accepts `--capacity-factor`,
`--pooled-transport-capacity-factor`, and `--num-expert-waves` to run
`--moe-impl fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`. The June `GrugModelConfig`
passes the latter two settings to the Grug MoE layer. Before building
any state, the benchmark rejects a missing transport factor or a wave
count that does not divide the local expert count. At batch 64 with 1
wave, pooled-wave took 2.459 s per step versus 2.427 s for ring
([results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6027494656),
jobs 453584, 453635, 453658). The pooled-wave validation was added after
these runs and has not been rerun on GPU.

The Slurm wrapper used for these runs is in #9877, and the collective
bandwidth benchmark is in #9886.

Part of #9812

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[experiments] Turn off allocator preallocation in the HPC Fund wrapper (#9901)

run_gpu.sh now exports XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false unless the
caller sets it, and the README lists the failure under known issues.

With preallocation, the BFC allocator pool is one fixed range. XLA
returns a step's large temp buffer to the pool while the step is still
running. A small buffer allocated in that window can land right after
the temp and stay live. The next step's temp is then 1 KiB larger than
the free space before that buffer and does not fit after it either.
Steps with 94-97 GiB temps hit this around step 5: batch 96 with
reference attention, and ring_dedup with save_moe at batch 64. Without
preallocation the pool grows by region.

A forced reproduction that keeps such small buffers alive ran out of
memory on 7-8 of 8 GPUs in each of two runs with preallocation. Three
runs without it passed. Step time is unchanged: 3.35 s at batch 96 with
reference attention and 1.58 s for ring_dedup with save_moe. Flash
attention at batch 96 with save_moe still fits at 235.8 GiB.

Part of #9812
